entities.name: Murasaki Shikibu
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Japanese noblewoman and lady-in-waiting at the Heian court (c. 973–c. 1014/1025 CE), author of The Tale of Genji — widely acclaimed as the world's first novel and the masterpiece of Japanese literature. Born into the Fujiwara clan, she received an unusually thorough literary education (including Chinese classics, normally reserved for men) and served at the court of Empress Shoshi.

Her diary (Murasaki Shikibu Diary) provides vivid glimpses of Heian court life. Her achievement is singular: in an era when European literature had not yet progressed beyond heroic epics and saints' lives, she produced a psychologically nuanced, aesthetically sophisticated novel of manners that remains profoundly moving a millennium later.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Murasaki Shikibu's novel, The Tale of Genji, is widely regarded as the world's first novel and a masterpiece of Japanese literature. Its influence on literary history and its enduring impact on Japanese culture make it a significant cultural artifact.
